{"concepts_used":["GC-0072","GC-0084","GC-0088","GC-0130","GC-0081","GC-0065","GC-0154"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part19B/4/4/2","quote":"Under subsection 120(3), a registered owner of a well known trade mark can take infringement action against a person who uses, as a trade mark, a substantially identical or deceptively similar sign in relation to goods or services unrelated to those in respect of which the well known trade mark is registered."},{"ref":"TMM/Part19B/4/4/2","quote":"The registered owner will be required to establish that, because the trade mark is well known, use of the sign would be likely to be taken as indicating a connection between the unrelated goods or services and the registered owner and for this reason the interests of the registered owner are likely to be adversely affected."}],"answer":"The interests affected are those of the registered owner of the well-known trade mark. The owner must establish that:
1. Because the mark is well known, use of the sign would likely be taken as indicating a connection between the unrelated goods or services and the registered owner; and
2. Because of that connection, the registered owner’s interests are likely to be adversely affected. [TMM/Part19B/4/4/2]

The Manual describes this protection as applying where another person uses, as a trade mark, a substantially identical or deceptively similar sign on unrelated goods or services. [TMM/Part19B/4/4/2]

Source distinction: this is the Manual’s account of subsection 120(3), not a quotation from the Act itself. The text of subsection 120(3) has not been supplied."}
